results.question: What is the waiting period for pregnancy?
results.answer: The waiting period for Pregnancy and birth services is 12 months. The mother needs to have served this full 12 months before Medibank can pay towards any hospital admissions for these services, and this applies regardless of the baby's due date or whether you were already pregnant when you took out or upgraded your cover. Pregnancy and birth services aren't covered on every product, so it's a good idea to check your Cover Summary or contact Medibank to make sure your cover includes them. Once your baby is born, remember to add them to your cover from birth in case they need hospital treatment straight away.

results.question: What is the waiting period for a pre-existing condition on hospital cover?
results.answer: Treatment of a pre-existing condition (PEC) on hospital cover has a 12-month waiting period. The exceptions are psychiatric care, rehabilitation and palliative care, which have a two-month waiting period even if the condition is pre-existing. Pregnancy and birth services always have a 12-month waiting period. A condition counts as pre-existing if, in the opinion of a Medibank-appointed Medical Practitioner, its signs or symptoms existed in the six months before you joined or changed your cover, even if it hadn't been diagnosed. The 12-month PEC wait also applies if you upgrade to cover with higher benefits for that treatment, so check your Cover Summary for details specific to your policy.

results.question: How long do I wait before I can claim general dental on extras?
results.answer: General dental isn't listed separately in the waiting periods, so it falls under 'All Treatment', which has a two month waiting period. Major dental work (such as endodontic treatment, surgical extractions, surgical procedures, orthodontics and all major dental services) has a longer 12 month waiting period. These apply where relevant to your cover, and some covers may have different rules, so please check your Cover Summary to confirm what's included and the waiting periods for your extras.

results.question: Can I suspend my membership while I travel overseas?
results.answer:
Yes, you can apply to suspend your membership while travelling overseas. A few things to know:
• You must apply before you leave, and you need to be away from Australia for at least two months (up to a maximum of four years).
• No benefits are paid for treatment, services or items during the suspension, and the suspended time doesn't count towards waiting periods or benefit replacement periods.
• If you have both Hospital and Extras cover, you can't suspend one without the other, and standalone Ambulance Cover can't be suspended.
• You'll need to wait at least six months after reactivating before suspending again for overseas travel, and you may need to provide supporting documents. You may also be subject to the Medicare Levy Surcharge while suspended.
Suspension is only available on eligible covers, and ahm memberships have different rules, so please check your Cover Summary.

results.question: Is there a cooling off period if I change my mind after joining?
results.answer: Yes. You have 30 days from the date your new or changed cover starts to make sure you're happy with it. If you change your mind within that time and haven't made any claims, Medibank can either move you to a more suitable cover from your original start date or cancel your cover and give you a full refund of the premiums you've paid. Just note that during the cooling off period you generally can't switch back to a cover that Medibank has closed.

results.question: How far in advance can I pay my premiums?
results.answer: Generally, you can pay your premiums up to 12 months in advance. If you have standalone Ambulance Cover, you can only pay either six or 12 months in advance. If a payment would take your cover more than 12 months ahead of the payment date, Medibank may refuse it or refund the excess portion. A handy bonus of paying ahead is premium protection: if premiums rise, the new rate usually won't apply until your next payment is due, unless you change things like your cover level or membership category.

results.question: How long do I have to submit a claim after my treatment?
results.answer: You should lodge your claim within two years of the date of your treatment, as Medibank can refuse to pay benefits for claims lodged more than two years after the date of service. For hospital stays, Medibank usually pays the hospital directly, so you often won't need to submit a separate claim. If you're claiming for an accident under Accident Cover Boost or the Accident waiting period waiver, note that benefits only apply to hospital treatment received within 12 months of the accident, and you'll need to submit an Accident form. Check your Cover Summary for details that apply to your specific cover.

results.question: If I switch from another health fund, do I have to serve waiting periods again?
results.answer:
Generally no, as long as you join Medibank within two months of leaving your previous fund. You'll usually only need to serve waiting periods for:
• treatments or items that weren't covered under your previous cover
• services with a higher benefit than before (e.g. upgrading from Restricted to Included, or a higher extras annual limit). Until you've served the new waiting period, benefits are paid at your old level if you'd already served it there
• any waiting periods you hadn't fully finished with your old fund
• everything, if your break in cover is more than two months, because you'll be treated as a new member
Also note that extras benefits paid by your previous fund count towards your annual limits in your first calendar year, your lifetime limits and benefit replacement periods, and loyalty bonuses from your old fund won't carry over. Check your Cover Summary for the waiting periods that apply to your cover.

results.question: Is ambulance covered by my hospital or extras cover?
results.answer: Ambulance services are covered under most Medibank Hospital and Extras covers, but it depends on your specific product, so please check your Cover Summary to confirm. If you're in NSW or the ACT and have Hospital cover, a government ambulance levy is included in your premium, which entitles you to ambulance services under your state/territory scheme. In that case, send any ambulance account to Medibank and we'll forward it to the ambulance service provider for payment. Medibank also offers standalone Ambulance Cover (not available in Queensland or Tasmania) if your current cover doesn't include it.

results.question: What is a benefit replacement period?
results.answer: A benefit replacement period is a set amount of time you need to wait from the date you bought an item before you can claim a benefit to replace it with another of the same type. It's separate from the waiting period for that item. Depending on your cover, it can apply per member or per membership, and benefits aren't payable for an item still within its replacement period. Check your Cover Summary to see which items on your cover have a benefit replacement period.

results.question: How do I add my newborn baby to my membership?
results.answer:
To add your baby, just contact Medibank, and it's best to add them from their date of birth so they're covered if they need hospital care in their own right (e.g. special care nursery or intensive care). Here's what to know:
- Single membership: apply within two months of birth. Your cover will change to a family or single parent family cover, backdated to the birth date, with higher premiums from then.
- Couple or family membership: apply within 12 months of birth to backdate cover to the birth date. After 12 months, cover starts from the application date.
- If your membership started no later than the birth and you add your baby on time, they only serve waiting periods you haven't already served. A child added to a single membership after two months must serve all waiting periods.
- If your baby isn't added in time, you'll be responsible for any costs of their hospital admission. With twins or other multiple births, the second and later babies are always admitted as inpatients, so adding them is especially important.

Your exact options depend on your membership type, so check your Cover Summary.

results.question: What is Lifetime Health Cover loading?
results.answer: Lifetime Health Cover (LHC) loading is an Australian government initiative to encourage people to take out Hospital cover before age 31. If you don't hold hospital cover by 1 July following your 31st birthday (your 'LHC base day'), you'll pay an extra 2% on your hospital premium for each year (or part year) you're aged over 30 when you take out cover, up to a maximum of 70%. For example, someone taking out Hospital cover for the first time at 55 would pay a 50% loading. The loading is removed once you've held hospital cover and paid the loading for 10 continuous years.

results.question: How do I make a claim for extras?
results.answer:
Here's how you can claim for extras:
• At the provider: most extras providers let you claim electronically with your membership card. The claim is processed on the spot and you just pay the remaining balance.
• Online: if on-the-spot claiming isn't available, you can submit most extras claims through your My Medibank account.
• By post: download a claim form from medibank.com.au and send it with your original invoices or receipts. These won't be returned, so keep a copy.
• Some items or services may need supporting documents. Some appliances, such as hearing devices or blood pressure monitors, also need a referral.
What you can claim and the benefits paid depend on your Extras cover, so check your Cover Summary.

results.question: What happens if I fall behind on my premium payments?
results.answer: If your premiums aren't paid up to date, your membership is considered to be in arrears. While you're in arrears, you won't receive any benefits for services provided or items bought during that time. If your premiums stay in arrears for more than two consecutive months, your membership may be closed and you'd no longer be eligible for any benefits. Premiums are payable in advance, and it's your responsibility to keep payments up to date, so you may want to set up a direct debit (bank or credit card) to help avoid falling behind.

results.question: What does the accident waiting period waiver mean?
results.answer: If your Hospital cover has a one-day or two-month waiting period for a service, Medibank may waive it (at its discretion) for treatment you need because of an Accident that happens during that waiting period. An Accident means an unforeseen event caused by an external force or object that results in an injury needing immediate treatment; it doesn't include illnesses with medical causes, pre-existing conditions, pregnancy or problems arising from surgery. All other waiting periods still apply. To claim, you'll need to submit an Accident form, which you can download at medibank.com.au. Check your Cover Summary for the waiting periods on your cover.

results.question: What about for extras like dental?
results.answer:
For Medibank extras (General Treatment) cover, waiting periods for dental depend on the type of treatment:
- General dental treatment falls under 'All Treatment', which has a two-month waiting period.
- Major dental services, including endodontic treatment (e.g. root canals), surgical extractions, surgical procedures and orthodontics, have a 12-month waiting period.
- Waiting periods apply when you first join, are added to a membership, upgrade to include new services or higher limits, or return after a break of two months or more, and no benefits are paid for services received during a waiting period.
What applies to you depends on your specific cover, so please check your Cover Summary.

results.question: I'm expecting a baby in a few months, when will my cover pay for the birth?
results.answer: Medibank can only pay towards hospital admissions for the birth once the mother has served a 12-month waiting period on a cover that includes Pregnancy and birth services. This applies no matter when your baby is due, and even if you were already pregnant when you took out or upgraded your cover. So whether the birth will be covered depends on whether your cover includes Pregnancy and birth services and when that waiting period started, so please check your Cover Summary or contact Medibank to confirm. Once your baby arrives, add them to your membership from their date of birth (within 2 months for a single membership, or 12 months for a couple or family membership) so they're covered if they need hospital care.
